measures.id: City of St. Petersburg No. 1 Referendum Question
measures.title: Stormwater, Wastewater and/or Potable Water Improvements General Obligation Bond Referendum
measures.summary: Asks whether the City may issue general obligation bonds of up to $600,000,000, maturing in no more than 30 years, to pay for storm resilience improvements such as floodwater protection, stormwater pump stations and drainage, plus wastewater and drinking water facilities. The bonds would be backed by the City's full faith, credit and unlimited property taxing power.
measures.yesMeans: The City may issue up to $600 million in general obligation bonds for storm, wastewater and drinking water improvements.
measures.noMeans: The City may not issue these general obligation bonds.

measures.id: City of St. Petersburg No. 1 Charter Amendment
measures.title: Removing City-Owned Vacant Lots from Park and Waterfront Map to Create Housing
measures.summary: The City Charter's Park and Waterfront Map includes a "Jamestown" parcel made up of Unity Park, open space at the Jamestown apartments, and nine vacant City-owned lots closed to the public. This amendment would remove those nine vacant lots from the map so that separate land use changes and a possible sale of the lots for affordable or workforce housing could follow.
measures.yesMeans: The nine vacant Jamestown lots are removed from the Charter's Park and Waterfront Map.
measures.noMeans: The nine lots stay on the Park and Waterfront Map.

measures.id: City of St. Petersburg No. 2 Referendum Question
measures.title: Authorizing Amendment of Harborage Marina Lease to Extend Term to 30 Years and Require Improvements
measures.summary: Asks whether City Council may amend the lease of City-owned submerged lands at Harborage Marina under the conditions in ordinance 640-H. The amendment would extend the lease to 30 years and require the tenant to build new improvements at no cost to the City, including 200 linear feet of docks, boat lifts and expanded restrooms, which the City would own when the lease ends.
measures.yesMeans: City Council may extend the Harborage Marina lease to 30 years with the required tenant-built improvements.
measures.noMeans: City Council may not approve this lease amendment.

measures.id: City of St. Petersburg No. 2 Charter Amendment
measures.title: Authorizing a 25-year Lease Limitation for the Port of St. Petersburg
measures.summary: The City Charter now limits leases at the Port of St. Petersburg to 10 years unless approved by a citywide referendum. This amendment would raise that limit to 25 years, matching the adjacent Albert Whitted Airport. It would not change the permitted use of the Port.
measures.yesMeans: Port of St. Petersburg leases of up to 25 years could be made without a citywide referendum.
measures.noMeans: The 10-year limit on Port leases without a referendum stays in place.

measures.id: City of St. Petersburg No. 3 Charter Amendment
measures.title: Technical, Clarifying, and Conforming Changes to Effectuate Holding Municipal Elections in Even-Numbered Years
measures.summary: In 2022, city voters approved moving Mayor and City Council elections to even-numbered years to align with state and national elections. This amendment would make technical, clarifying and conforming changes to the Charter to carry out that decision, including aligning the Charter-review process with the current election schedule.
measures.yesMeans: The Charter is updated with technical changes to match the even-year election schedule.
measures.noMeans: The Charter is not changed with these technical updates.
